note.en: What you see: This protocol turns the cava view into a fluid decision. In a spontaneously breathing patient the cava collapses on inspiration when venous pressure is low and stays fixed and plump when pressure is high. A small cava with big collapse predicts that fluids will raise output, while a large fixed cava warns that more fluid may harm. The scan always pairs with lungs, blood pressure trend and examination, since no single vessel decides resuscitation alone.

steps.en: What you see: This protocol turns the cava view into a fluid decision. In a spontaneously breathing patient the cava collapses on inspiration when venous pressure is low and stays fixed and plump when pressure is high. A small cava with big collapse predicts that fluids will raise output, while a large fixed cava warns that more fluid may harm. The scan always pairs with lungs, blood pressure trend and examination, since no single vessel decides resuscitation alone.
Landmarks to confirm: Inferior vena cava trunk at 1 to 2 cm from the junction, right atrium entry, bilateral lung zones for B line monitoring.

Common mistakes and correction: Measuring a hepatic branch instead of the trunk: track to the atrial entry first. Oblique beam overstating collapse: keep perpendicular. Applying the sniff rule to a ventilated patient: ventilation reverses the pattern, so seek senior guidance instead.

Normal values with units: Diameter 2.1 cm or less with collapse above 50 percent on sniff marks right atrial pressure of 0 to 5 mmHg and predicts fluid tolerance. Diameter above 2.1 cm with collapse below 50 percent marks pressure of 10 to 20 mmHg and warns against large volumes. New B lines after fluids mean stop even when the cava still collapses.

Pitfalls: Raised abdominal pressure, severe tricuspid regurgitation and right heart failure all distend the cava regardless of true volume. In circulatory failure with lung injury, even small volumes can wetten the lungs, so monitor breathing continuously. Record numbers with the clinical context so the reviewer sees the full picture.

todo.en: How to get it step by step: Obtain the cava in sagittal through the liver and measure 1 to 2 cm from the atrial junction. Record M mode across a full breath with a sniff. Calculate collapse as the fall in diameter over the maximum, expressed as a percent. Scan the lungs for B lines before and after any fluid challenge. Reassess the cava after each challenge and stop fluids when the collapse normalises or lungs wetten.
